scientific_queries.note: All-cell leave-one-out with m up to 400, to settle where personalisation turns positive.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round replaces a 12-cell design with an all-cell one and finds the opposite of the earlier positive result, then explains the conflict.

the_conflict_with_R76.R76: with a marginal prior at about 7%, personalisation helped (+1.64 pp at m=100, +2.62 pp at m=200, both significant)
the_conflict_with_R76.R111: with marginal priors at 12-13% and combined priors near 17%, personalisation hurts at every m from 150 to 400, all eight intervals significantly negative
the_conflict_with_R76.likely_resolution: the sign depends on prior strength: a weak prior benefits from noisy per-drug corrections because they carry information, a strong prior only absorbs their noise
the_conflict_with_R76.honest_caveat: prior strength was not manipulated. It differs partly because the pool-size requirements differ (600 versus 840 keys), which selects different cells, so it is a concomitant variable rather than a control

limits: only 48 of 125 cells meet the 840-key requirement
the evaluation set shrinks as m grows because measured keys are removed
per-drug residuals at these m values rest on few keys per drug, which is the mechanism but also makes the result sensitive to how residuals are estimated
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: explicitly manipulate prior strength on a fixed cell set, for example by weakening the prior deliberately, and check whether the sign of personalisation crosses over

register_updates.C84: new: personalisation is significantly harmful when the prior is strong, and the R76 conflict points to prior strength as a hidden variable
